answer.rationale: Primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line runs at 94% with no buffer, so deferral or adding a second source without securing the incumbent would create a supply cliff (c5 applied only to a non-critical month-to-month case). Switching primary would raise delivery risk in this window despite last year's cost win. Incumbent continuity historically protected integration and deliveries (c1). Negotiation at renewal previously moved price and terms (c4) and multi-year volume commitments cut unit cost without narrowing service (c6), which is the only path that can pursue the 18% spend cut without increasing delivery risk. Those memories are from other cycles and do not quantify an 18% cut here, so the size of the attainable saving remains uncertain. Downstream assembly disruption risk is flagged.
